authorities.authority: DoT — Department of Telecommunications (own website: licensing/circulars/OMs, non-Gazette stream)
authorities.url: https://www.dot.gov.in/whatsnew (also /circulars, /access-services licensing pages; instrument PDFs at /static/uploads/ and /sites/default/files/)
authorities.instrument_types: Licence amendments (Unified Licence / UL-VNO / access / ISP / ILD), amendments to licence conditions, office memoranda, circulars, clarifications, public notices, LoIs, M&A/transfer approvals, press releases
authorities.binds_whom: All licensed telcos, ISPs, VNOs, ILDOs, infra providers — i.e. the core of the telecom client base
authorities.notes: This is the single biggest hole in my slice. We catch DoT ONLY via ministry-wise Gazette (Communications). A large share of obligation-changing DoT output — licence-condition amendments, OMs, clarifications, LoIs, procedural circulars — is published on dot.gov.in and NOT gazetted, or lands on the site days/weeks before the Gazette catches up. Site is a Next.js SPA so the listing needs a headless render / backend-API discovery, but the actual PDFs are static and directly fetchable (verified HTTP 200, 4MB PDF at /static/uploads/2025/07/…). robots.txt = 'Allow: /'. Recent proof: July 2025 NSDTS Annexure-A PDF; the rolling Telecom Act 2023 rule/clarification drafts posted for comment. A telecom partner would be embarrassed to learn of a UL amendment from a client rather than from the tracker.

authorities.authority: WPC — Wireless Planning & Coordination Wing (incl. ETA / import licensing / frequency / NFAP)
authorities.instrument_types: Equipment Type Approval (ETA, incl. self-declaration), import licences, frequency assignment / NOCs, dealer possession licences, de-licensing notifications, National Frequency Allocation Plan (NFAP), amateur/experimental licences
authorities.binds_whom: Device/handset/IoT/short-range-device makers and importers, telcos, tower cos, satcom earth-station operators — anyone importing or radiating RF
authorities.notes: Not in the source list and a genuine miss for a broad TMT practice with device/OEM clients. WPC governs whether hardware can lawfully be imported or sold. ETA now largely self-declaration on the DoT eServices/Saral Sanchar portal (Rs 10,000/model via Bharatkosh); de-licensing decisions (e.g. lower-6 GHz Wi-Fi delicensing consultation, low-power/very-low-power device bands) and NFAP revisions are the obligation-movers. De-licensing notifications also hit the Gazette (so partially gazette-recoverable), but ETA lists, import-licence procedure and WPC notices are website/portal-only. wpc.dot.gov.in itself now times out — the function has migrated into dot.gov.in + eservices.dot.gov.in.

authorities.authority: DoT Spectrum Management — auction NIAs & spectrum administration
authorities.instrument_types: Notice Inviting Applications (NIA) for auctions + corrigenda, auction rules/reserve prices/pre-qualification, spectrum trading / sharing / surrender / harmonisation approvals, backhaul & administrative-assignment orders (incl. satcom spectrum)
authorities.binds_whom: All telcos and new entrants; satcom operators once satellite spectrum is assigned administratively
authorities.notes: Final allotments are gazetted (caught), but the NIA itself, its corrigenda, and pre-bid clarifications live on dot.gov.in/spectrum and PIB, not the Gazette — and these set the terms clients bid on. Recent proof: NIA of 08-Mar-2024 (10,523 MHz, reserve ~Rs 96,317 cr, auction 25-Jun-2024) published on dot.gov.in/spectrum with deadline extensions issued as web corrigenda. The live satcom-spectrum pricing question (TRAI recommendations -> DoT administrative assignment) will surface here first. PIB (Ministry of Communications) is the fastest signal but not itself a binding-instrument issuer.

authorities.authority: Trusted Telecom Portal / National Security Directive on Telecom Sector (NCSC + DoT)
authorities.instrument_types: Trusted-source / trusted-product designations, designated-source (no-procurement) lists, portal instructions and licence-condition amendments giving the NSDTS effect
authorities.binds_whom: All TSPs — mandatory to procure only trusted products for network expansion/upgrades
authorities.notes: Distinct from NCCS (which we cover for MTCTE/ITSAR security testing). This is supply-chain trust: TSPs must connect only 'trusted products' designated via this portal. The specific source/product designations are largely login-gated and the sensitive no-procurement decisions are effectively unpublished/confidential — a partner learns of them via portal notices, licence-amendment OMs on dot.gov.in, and client channels, not a clean public feed. What IS trackable: the public brief and the periodic DoT amendments operationalising it (e.g. July 2025 NSDTS Annexure-A PDF on dot.gov.in). Worth adding for the public layer; flag the designation lists as genuinely unpublished.

authorities.authority: Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) — formerly USOF
authorities.instrument_types: DBN scheme guidelines, funding/subsidy notices, bidding documents (BharatNet, mobile-coverage schemes), administrator circulars
authorities.binds_whom: TSPs / infra providers / BharatNet contractors bidding for or receiving rural-connectivity support
authorities.notes: Now a statutory fund under the Telecommunications Act 2023 (ss.24-26), rebranded from USOF to Digital Bharat Nidhi — a live 2024-2025 event that itself proves the source moved and matters. Site is clean static HTML (~221KB, verified 200) so easily harvestable — no JS barrier, unlike dot.gov.in. Scheme guidelines and bidding terms directly set obligations for anyone touching BharatNet / rural rollout. Missing entirely.

authorities.authority: SACFA — Standing Advisory Committee on Frequency Allocation (WPC sub-committee)
authorities.url: https://www.dot.gov.in/spectrummanagement (guidelines); clearances transacted via https://eservices.dot.gov.in/ (Saral Sanchar)
authorities.instrument_types: SACFA siting clearances, clearance procedure/guideline circulars, height/EMI-EMC and location conditions
authorities.binds_whom: Tower companies, telcos, satcom earth-station and VSAT operators, large private-network/CUG deployers
authorities.notes: The gating clearance for physically installing antennae/towers/earth stations. Individual clearances are transactional (per-site, via portal), so the trackable layer is the procedure/guideline circulars and any streamlining notices (relevant to 5G small-cells and street-furniture deployment). Folds operationally into WPC/DoT but a practitioner names it separately because infra clients ask about it by name.

authorities.authority: Right of Way (RoW) / GatiShakti Sanchar portal (DoT)
authorities.url: RoW Rules via Gazette; DoT RoW circulars at dot.gov.in; portal at https://eservices.dot.gov.in/gss
authorities.instrument_types: RoW Rules (now under Telecom Act 2023) and amendments, RoW clarificatory circulars/OMs, dispute-resolution and fee/timeline notifications; GatiShakti Sanchar single-window portal (transactional)
authorities.binds_whom: TSPs and infrastructure providers laying OFC / erecting towers; state RoW nodal officers
authorities.notes: The RoW Rules themselves are gazetted (caught via gazette_communications), but DoT's RoW clarificatory circulars, model-timeline OMs and portal-integration notices are website-only and are the practical obligation-movers for rollout. The GatiShakti Sanchar portal (eservices.dot.gov.in/gss, Jan Parichay SSO) is transactional, not an instrument feed. New Telecom-Act RoW rules and the drive to make all states live on the portal by 2025 are the current activity. Add the DoT RoW-circulars layer; the portal itself is not a harvest target.

authorities.authority: DoT eServices / Saral Sanchar — registrations (OSP, M2M/WPAN, ISP, ILD, PM-WANI)
authorities.instrument_types: OSP (Other Service Provider / BPO) registration terms & revised guidelines, M2M service-provider & WPAN/WLAN registration, ISP/ILD/CUG registration conditions, public notices attached to the portal
authorities.binds_whom: BPO/ITES and shared-services OSPs, M2M/IoT and telematics providers, ISPs — a big slice of a broad TMT client roster
authorities.notes: Registration is transactional, but the guidelines governing it change obligations for whole client classes (the 2020-2022 OSP liberalisation is the archetype; M2M/embedded-SIM registration is the live one). Guideline revisions usually also appear as DoT circulars/Gazette, so partly caught upstream — but the eServices portal is where the operative terms and public notices actually surface. Lower rank than WPC/spectrum but a real gap for the enterprise/BPO side of the practice.

authorities.authority: PM-WANI (Public Wi-Fi framework; DoT / C-DOT central registry)
authorities.url: https://pmwani.gov.in/ (framework instruments on dot.gov.in / Gazette; registration via Saral Sanchar)
authorities.instrument_types: PM-WANI framework amendments, PDO/PDOA/App-Provider registration terms, central-registry app-provider approvals
authorities.binds_whom: Public Data Office Aggregators, PDOs, PM-WANI app providers; ISPs supplying bandwidth
authorities.notes: Niche-to-moderate: matters to public-Wi-Fi and aggregator clients. Framework changes ride TRAI recommendations + DoT notifications (partly caught upstream via TRAI/Gazette), so the standalone registry adds mainly registration terms and app-provider approvals. Track only if the practice has public-Wi-Fi clients; otherwise low priority.

authorities.authority: Digital Communications Commission (DCC) — apex DoT body (ex-Telecom Commission)
authorities.url: No standalone site; decisions surface via dot.gov.in press releases / notifications
authorities.instrument_types: Policy and spectrum-pricing approvals, licence-framework decisions (announced, then executed as DoT notifications)
authorities.binds_whom: All telecom licensees (indirectly, through the DoT instruments that implement DCC decisions)
authorities.notes: Not a separate feed — the DCC decides, then DoT/the Gazette issues the operative instrument. Adequately captured once the DoT own-website stream (row 1) is added; no independent harvest target. Listed so it is not mistaken for an uncovered authority.

authorities.authority: Department of Space / Indian Space Policy (DoS) — satcom policy layer above IN-SPACe
authorities.instrument_types: Indian Space Policy 2023 and successor policy documents, DoS/IN-SPACe overarching guidelines feeding satcom authorisation
authorities.binds_whom: Satellite operators, NGSO/GSO constellation applicants, satcom service providers (via IN-SPACe authorisation + DoT/WPC spectrum)
authorities.notes: The operative satcom authoriser — IN-SPACe — is already covered, and DoT/WPC handle spectrum. DoS/ISRO add the policy backdrop (Indian Space Policy 2023) rather than client-binding instruments, so this is a moderate/niche top-up, not a core gap. Track the policy page only if the satcom practice needs the upstream signal.

authorities.authority: C-DOT / NTIPRIT / TERM cells (DoT field & attached units)
authorities.url: https://www.cdot.in/ ; TERM cells operate internally under DoT LSAs
authorities.instrument_types: C-DOT standards/reference designs (PM-WANI, interception), NTIPRIT training notes, TERM-cell EMF-compliance and enforcement actions
authorities.binds_whom: Vendors interfacing with C-DOT standards; licensees on EMF/enforcement (TERM)
authorities.notes: Genuinely low priority. TERM-cell enforcement (EMF self-certification, subscriber-verification audits) can change a licensee's operational obligations, but the instruments are internal/LSA-level and effectively unpublished — a partner learns of them via client notices and DoT circulars, not a public feed. C-DOT is R&D, not a regulator. Note for completeness; do not build a scraper for it.

authorities.authority: MeitY — Ministry of Electronics and IT (direct site: Orders & Notices, Gazette Notifications, Acts & Policies, Guidelines via meity.gov.in WP-JSON API)
authorities.instrument_types: IT Rules 2021 Part II amendments, SSMI additional due-diligence notifications, s.79 due-diligence advisories, deepfake/synthetic-media & GenAI advisories, GAC constitution/reconstitution notifications, draft rules issued for consultation, office memoranda, press notes
authorities.binds_whom: all intermediaries incl. Significant Social Media Intermediaries (social platforms, messaging), and via advisories AI/GenAI platforms and app stores
authorities.notes: The single highest-value gap in this slice and the most embarrassing to miss. e-Gazette (gazette_meity, live) catches the FINAL notified rule — e.g. the IT (Intermediary Guidelines) Amendment Rules 2026 on synthetically generated information, in force 20 Feb 2026 — so notified rules are not lost. What is lost is everything MeitY posts on its own site but never gazettes: the pre-notification SGI DRAFT (22 Oct 2025), the Nov-2023/Mar-2024 deepfake advisories, GenAI advisories, s.79 letters, and GAC/blocking administrative notices, which live only under meity.gov.in 'Orders & Notices' / PIB. Verified: the WP-JSON API returns clean JSON and robots is 'Allow: /'. Crucially the 4 meity_* endpoints are ALREADY discovered in registry_v2.json but parked at status 'needs_decision' (not live) — promoting them to live is the top action.

authorities.authority: MHA / I4C — Sahyog portal (s.79(3)(b) content-removal notices)
authorities.instrument_types: s.79(3)(b) takedown/removal notices routed from authorized central/state agencies and police to intermediaries; onboarding and nodal-officer directions
authorities.binds_whom: every intermediary onboarded to Sahyog (X/Twitter, Meta, Google/YouTube, and all notified platforms)
authorities.notes: THE live intermediary-liability battleground of 2025. Karnataka HC (Nagaprasanna J.), X Corp v Union of India, 24 Sept 2025 (351 pp), UPHELD the Sahyog portal, Rule 3(1)(d) and the s.79(3)(b) blocking power against X's argument that only s.69A can block; X Corp filed a writ appeal on 14 Nov 2025. The notices themselves are structurally untrackable — sahyog.mha.gov.in returned http 000 (closed to non-onboarded), notices are visible only to the served intermediary. Trackable proxies only: the enabling Rule 3(1)(d) (gazette-recoverable), MHA/PIB press, and the client being served. Flag as a monitored blind spot, not a scrapeable feed.

authorities.authority: Grievance Appellate Committee(s) (GAC) — MeitY (Rule 3A, IT Rules 2021)
authorities.instrument_types: appellate orders reviewing intermediary grievance-officer decisions (content takedown/retention, account suspension/removal)
authorities.binds_whom: all intermediaries — statutorily bound to comply with GAC orders under Rule 3A
authorities.notes: Three GACs, constituted by the Oct-2022 amendment, operational since 1 Mar 2023 — a large and growing body of de facto content-moderation precedent that binds every intermediary. Portal shows 60,147 appeals received / 11,197 disposed (fetched 27 Aug 2026). But there is NO public orders repository: each order is visible only to the appellant behind OTP + captcha login (bot-detection — must not be bypassed). No robots.txt, but a Terms of Service gate applies. The only public artefacts are the aggregate counters and the MeitY constitution/reconstitution notifications (gazette-recoverable). Genuine high-severity gap with no clean instrument feed; a partner learns of GAC reasoning from the client's own appeals and occasional press.

authorities.authority: MeitY Designated Officer + Inter-departmental Committee (s.69A blocking; IT Procedure and Safeguards for Blocking Rules 2009)
authorities.instrument_types: s.69A blocking directions to intermediaries/ISPs; Review Committee decisions; emergency blocking orders
authorities.binds_whom: intermediaries, ISPs and telcos served with blocking directions
authorities.notes: Confidential by design — Rule 16 of the 2009 Blocking Rules imposes strict confidentiality on requests and actions, so individual orders are published nowhere. This is central to the practice but is not a wireable web source: a partner learns of orders from the served client, from litigation (Shreya Singhal 2015; the Twitter/X v Union of India s.69A challenge, Karnataka HC 2023), from RTI, and from aggregate figures in Parliament answers and MeitY press. The 2009 Blocking Rules text is gazette-recoverable; the orders are not. Record explicitly as a known structural blind spot so it is not mistaken for coverage.

authorities.authority: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) / Ministry of Home Affairs
authorities.instrument_types: cyber advisories/alerts, blocking recommendations that feed s.69A app/URL bans, SOPs and directions to intermediaries, mule-account / 'digital arrest' / betting-&-loan-app advisories
authorities.binds_whom: intermediaries, payment & UPI intermediaries, and app stores — indirectly via notices, blocking recommendations and onboarding demands
authorities.notes: I4C is the operational engine behind Sahyog and much of the s.69A app-blocking wave (it drove blocking of thousands of URLs and betting/loan apps across 2024-25). i4c.mha.gov.in is reachable static HTML but thin on instruments; the sister citizen portal cybercrime.gov.in returned an 'Unauthorised Access' wall to non-browser requests, so treat it as terms-restricted. Most of I4C's client-relevant output actually surfaces through PIB rather than its own sites, which argues for capturing it via the PIB signal lane.

authorities.authority: Press Information Bureau (PIB) — MeitY / MHA releases feed
authorities.instrument_types: government press releases announcing app bans, s.69A blocking counts, advisories and rule notifications (signal source, not a primary instrument publisher)
authorities.binds_whom: no direct binding effect — the tripwire that surfaces MeitY/MHA/I4C action affecting intermediaries before or instead of any published instrument
authorities.notes: Frequently the ONLY public trace of a s.69A blocking action or app ban, and the first surfacing of drafts (e.g. the Oct-2025 SGI draft press note). Already discovered in registry_v2.json as pib_moc but parked at status 'needs_decision' (not live). pib.gov.in is already in the robots snapshot and the RSS feed is clean — a low-cost, high-value signal lane. Decide and enable; pair it with the MeitY-direct promotion to close most of the non-gazetted-advisory gap.

authorities.authority: PIB Fact Check Unit (FCU) — Rule 3(1)(b)(v), IT Rules 2021 (MeitY notified, MIB/PIB operated)
authorities.instrument_types: fact-check flags deeming government-related content 'fake/false/misleading' (mechanism struck down)
authorities.binds_whom: intermediaries — would have lost safe harbour over FCU-flagged content; now moot
authorities.notes: Included only to close the loop and prevent a false 'we should add this' impulse: the Rule 3(1)(b)(v) FCU amendment was struck down as unconstitutional by the Bombay High Court (Kunal Kamra v Union of India, tie-breaker judgment 20 Sept 2024). There is no live binding mechanism — do NOT wire a source. Keep only a watch note in case of legislative revival or a Digital India Act successor provision.

authorities.authority: MeitY (Ministry of Electronics & IT) — own website publications (advisories, AI guidelines, draft-rule consultations, office memoranda, press notes)
authorities.instrument_types: IT Act rules & amendments (gazetted), plus the non-gazetted layer that actually moves first: AI/due-diligence advisories, the India AI Governance Guidelines, draft rules put out for consultation, office memoranda, sectoral directions and press notes
authorities.binds_whom: Every intermediary, social media intermediary, SSMI, OTT/streaming, gaming, e-commerce and AI/GenAI deployer; and via DPDP, every data fiduciary
authorities.notes: This is the #1 embarrassing gap. We only have the Gazette-MeitY route, which catches gazetted rules (DPDP Rules notified 14 Nov 2025; IT Rules synthetic-content/deepfake 'SGI labelling' amendment notified 10 Feb 2026) — but MISSES the instruments that hit clients first and never touch the Gazette: the India AI Governance Guidelines (released 5 Nov 2025), the March 2024 GenAI due-diligence advisories, and consultation drafts (e.g. the Oct 2025 draft AI/deepfake rules, comments to 13 Nov 2025). Those are letters/guidelines/OMs on the MeitY site only. Site is a Next.js SPA (__NEXT_DATA__ JSON in-page; PDFs served static at /static/uploads/...); robots is 'Allow: /'. Scrape whats-new + document/notification listings and the PDF store. Highest-value add in this slice.

authorities.authority: Data Protection Board of India (DPBI)
authorities.url: https://www.meity.gov.in/ (Board has no standalone portal live yet — dpb.gov.in / dpbi.gov.in do not resolve)
authorities.instrument_types: Adjudication orders, directions to remediate/mitigate breaches, monetary penalties, and interim directions under the DPDP Act 2023 / DPDP Rules 2025
authorities.binds_whom: Every data fiduciary and Significant Data Fiduciary — i.e. effectively every TMT client processing personal data (platforms, telcos, adtech, SaaS, fintech, consent managers)
authorities.notes: No longer hypothetical: Board constituted 13 Nov 2025; Chairperson and Members appointed 6 June 2026, so first inquiries/penalties are imminent. This is the enforcement engine of DPDP and the single biggest FUTURE gap. The Rules make it 'digital by design', so a dedicated e-adjudication portal is expected — set a watch for it. Until then, constitution/appointments come via Gazette-MeitY and MeitY press; early orders will surface through MeitY and press before any portal. Track proactively; do not wait for the portal to appear.

authorities.authority: NCIIPC (National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre), s.70A IT Act
authorities.url: https://nciipc.gov.in/ (unreachable externally — ECONNREFUSED / walled to gov networks)
authorities.instrument_types: s.70 'protected system' designations (Gazette-notified), CII protection guidelines, sectoral advisories/vulnerability disclosures, and compliance under the IT (Information Security Practices for Protected System) Rules 2018
authorities.binds_whom: Any TMT entity whose infrastructure is designated CII — large telcos, data centres, cloud/hosting, submarine-cable and IXP operators, digital-payment rails
authorities.notes: Split source. The binding act — a s.70(1) protected-system designation — is a Gazette notification, so Gazette-MeitY partially catches it (worth an explicit NCIIPC/protected-system keyword filter on the Gazette feed). The NCIIPC site itself (its CII guidelines, RVDP advisories, threat notes) actively refuses external connections from our vantage — treat as not_online for crawling. A designation converts a client into a s.70-protected-system operator with audit/reporting duties, so missing one is material even though volume is low.

authorities.authority: UIDAI (Unique Identification Authority of India) — Aadhaar
authorities.instrument_types: Aadhaar (Authentication & Offline Verification) Regulations and amendments, circulars/directions to AUAs/KUAs/ASAs/Sub-AUAs, and eKYC/face-auth operational directions
authorities.binds_whom: Every Aadhaar-authentication user — telecom SIM onboarding, fintech/banking eKYC, DigiLocker-adjacent platforms, any TMT client doing Aadhaar-based verification
authorities.notes: As the practice already treats it, gazette-only for us: gazetted Aadhaar regulation amendments are recoverable via Gazette-MeitY (partial), but the UIDAI website's circulars/OMs to the auth ecosystem are missed — and the site is robots 'Disallow: /', so polite crawling is off-limits; the Gazette is the clean route. Recent proof it moves obligations: the 2025-26 face-authentication push and the revamped Aadhaar app / Good-Governance Aadhaar-sharing rules changed onboarding duties for AUAs. Keep on the gazette-recoverable watch with UIDAI/Aadhaar keyword filters.

authorities.authority: s.69A blocking regime — MeitY blocking committee under the IT (Blocking) Rules 2009
authorities.instrument_types: Content/URL/app blocking directions to intermediaries and telcos under s.69A
authorities.binds_whom: Social media intermediaries, ISPs/telcos, app stores, streaming and hosting providers
authorities.notes: Structurally untrackable at source: Rule 16 of the Blocking Rules 2009 makes these directions confidential, so there is no feed to scrape and no honest way to 'cover' them directly. Say so plainly. A partner actually learns of them from (a) the client intermediary that receives the order, (b) litigation — the X Corp v Union of India challenge in the Karnataka High Court (2025) to the s.79(3)(b)/Sahyog blocking practice is the live proof — and (c) platform transparency reports (X/Google) and press. Recommend a litigation/press signal rather than a source crawler.

authorities.authority: CCA (Controller of Certifying Authorities), s.17 IT Act
authorities.instrument_types: Interoperability Guidelines for DSC, Certificate Policy, Identity Verification Guidelines, SSL/e-Sign framework, PKI and CA-licensing/audit guidelines
authorities.binds_whom: Licensed Certifying Authorities, eSign ASPs/ESPs, trust-service and eKYC providers, and any TMT/fintech client relying on DSC/eSign for onboarding or document execution
authorities.notes: Clean and easy to add: plain static HTML, no robots.txt (404), PDFs at /sites/files/pdf/guidelines/. Actively maintained — Interoperability Guidelines for DSC (CCA-IOG), Identity Verification (CCA-IVG) and SSL-issuance (CCA-SSL) guidelines carry 2026 revision dates. Moderate rather than high for a broad TMT partner (matters most to fintech onboarding, eSign vendors and CAs), but it is a low-effort, defensible catch that rounds out the digital-trust corner of the slice.

authorities.authority: I4C (Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre), MHA
authorities.instrument_types: Advisories and directions on mule accounts, app/URL/website blocking, SIM/handset actions, and the 'Suspect Registry' — largely via letter-directions to intermediaries, telcos and banks
authorities.binds_whom: Social media and payment intermediaries, telcos, fintech/UPI players, app stores
authorities.notes: Boundary item (MHA, not MeitY) but rising fast and a broad TMT partner feels it — I4C is the operational hub behind mass app/URL blocking and mule-account/telecom actions (Sanchar Saathi/Chakshu adjacency). Much of what binds clients arrives as non-public letter-directions, so like s.69A it is only partly trackable; the site carries advisories/press worth a light crawl. Flag as an awareness/press signal, not a comprehensive source. Note also the DoT Telecom (Telecom Cyber Security) Rules 2024 sit at this boundary — likely the telecom analyst's lane, but confirm it is owned somewhere.

authorities.authority: CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team), s.70B IT Act
authorities.instrument_types: s.70B(6) Directions, security guidelines (CISG), advisories (CIAD), vulnerability notes (CIVN)
authorities.binds_whom: All body corporates, intermediaries, data centres, VPN/cloud providers, VDA exchanges — near-universal TMT reach
authorities.notes: Already fully covered across all four lanes (directions, CISG, CIAD, CIVN) — restated here as the anchor of the cyber corner so the map is complete. The load-bearing instrument remains the 28 Apr 2022 s.70B(6) Directions (6-hour incident reporting, 180-day log retention). No gap; keep the existing crawlers. Confirm the s.70B(6) directions lane keeps catching any fresh directions/FAQs, since new directions arrive irregularly and out of the advisory cadence.

authorities.authority: STQC (Standardisation Testing & Quality Certification Directorate), MeitY
authorities.instrument_types: Empanelment of information-security auditors, audit standards/GIGW conformity, and eSign/data-centre audit criteria
authorities.binds_whom: CII operators and data fiduciaries needing empanelled audits; eSign/ASP infrastructure; e-gov service providers
authorities.notes: Genuinely niche — STQC sets who can audit (empanelled auditor lists) and the conformity criteria that CII/DPDP/eSign audits are measured against, rather than issuing obligations directly. Relevant when advising on audit-vendor selection or GIGW conformance. Low priority; list it for completeness but do not prioritise over MeitY/DPBI/NCIIPC. (For context: there is still no statutory AI regulator — AI in this slice lives inside MeitY via advisories and the AI Governance Guidelines; the IndiaAI Mission / AI Safety Institute are capacity bodies, not rule-issuers, so nothing to crawl there yet.)

authorities.authority: CCPA — Central Consumer Protection Authority (Dept of Consumer Affairs)
authorities.instrument_types: Guidelines (Prevention of Misleading Advertisements & Endorsements 2022; Dark Patterns 2023), advisories, safety notices, and final orders/penalties under the Consumer Protection Act 2019
authorities.binds_whom: Every advertiser, manufacturer, service provider, endorser/influencer, ad agency, e-commerce platform, and any broadcaster/OTT/print outlet carrying the ad — the single broadest advertising-conduct regulator in the slice
authorities.notes: The biggest embarrassment gap. This is the statutory teeth behind advertising that ASCI (self-reg) lacks. Extremely live: June 2025 self-audit advisory on dark patterns (in force to 31 Dec 2026); nine platforms penalised over 2025-26 (Zepto, BookMyShow, IndiGo, PhysicsWallah, FirstCry, SpiceJet); new misleading-advertisement/endorsement guidelines flagged Mar 2026. Orders live at ccpa-orders.php and doca.gov.in/ccpa/orders-advisories.php; final-orders PDF served directly. Sits under DoCA — NOT captured by our Communications/MeitY/MIB gazette lanes, so genuinely invisible to us today.

authorities.authority: DPCGC — Digital Publisher Content Grievances Council (IAMAI Level-II SRB)
authorities.instrument_types: Level-II self-regulatory advisories, grievance/appeal decisions, and Code-of-Ethics guidance issued under IT (Intermediary Guidelines & Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules 2021, Part III
authorities.binds_whom: OTT / online curated-content publishers and digital news publishers that are IAMAI members — the SRB tier every OTT client answers to before MIB's Level-III steps in
authorities.notes: Critical for any OTT client but genuinely awkward to reach: dpcgc.in is a Squarespace 'Private Site' (meta noindex), and dpcgc.org returned HTTP 509 (bandwidth exceeded) — i.e. content is only semi-published, usually surfacing via press releases and PDF advisories rather than a clean index. Feb 2025 advisory told all OTTs to comply with the Code of Ethics and obscenity law; the July 2025 MIB blocking of 25 OTT apps is the enforcement backdrop that makes the SRB tier matter. A partner realistically tracks this via IAMAI press + trade media, not the site.

authorities.authority: NBDSA — News Broadcasting & Digital Standards Authority (NBDA)
authorities.instrument_types: Adjudicatory orders (with fines), advisories, and the NBDA's own News Broadcasting & Digital Standards Regulations/Guidelines
authorities.binds_whom: News-TV broadcasters that are NBDA members and — since the June 2025 Regulations amendment — their digital news operations
authorities.notes: Every news-broadcaster client tracks NBDSA orders closely; they set de-facto content standards ahead of any MIB action. 2025 run is heavy: nine orders on communal reporting/privacy (Zee News fined Rs 25,000); 9 Jun 2025 advisory on misleading tickers/thumbnails directing Times Now Navbharat to edit; NBDA amended its Regulations Jun 2025 to fold digital news under NBDSA. Orders index is clean static HTML; robots.txt blocks only /admin/ and /beta/.

authorities.authority: BCCC / IBDF — Broadcasting Content Complaints Council + Digital Media Content Regulatory Council (DMCRC)
authorities.instrument_types: BCCC decisions/orders and IBDF self-regulatory content guidelines for non-news TV; DMCRC (IBDF's Level-II OTT SRB) grievance decisions
authorities.binds_whom: General-entertainment (non-news) TV broadcasters that are IBDF members via BCCC; IBDF-member OTT platforms via DMCRC
authorities.notes: The GEC-TV counterpart to NBDSA and the IBDF-side OTT SRB — completes the self-reg map (NBDSA=news, BCCC=GEC TV, DPCGC/DMCRC=OTT). Live domain is ibdf.com (ibdf.org.in is dead); BCCC has published decisions since 2011 and the decisions page is public. bcccindia.org also resolves (robots fully permissive). Note the correction to the partner's shorthand: DPCGC is IAMAI's body, while IBDF's own OTT SRB is DMCRC — both are MIB-recognised Level-II bodies.

authorities.authority: MIB — IT Rules Part III Level-III / Inter-Departmental Committee + IT Act s.69A blocking orders
authorities.instrument_types: Inter-Departmental Committee recommendations, MIB Level-III oversight directions, and content-blocking orders under IT Act s.69A read with the Blocking Rules 2009
authorities.binds_whom: OTT / digital-news publishers and intermediaries — the government tier above the SRBs
authorities.notes: We capture MIB's public face (mib_orders_notices, mib_digital_media, gazette_mib), but the operative s.69A/Blocking orders are confidential under Rule 16 and are NOT published. The July 2025 blocking of 25 OTT apps is the live example: the order itself never surfaced — a partner learns of these only via MIB press release, the platform's own takedown notice, or a court record when litigated. Worth an explicit 'unpublished — track via press/litigation' note in the tracker so the gap is acknowledged rather than silently missed.

authorities.authority: CBC — Central Bureau of Communication (formerly DAVP)
authorities.instrument_types: Empanelment policy, advertising rate cards / periodic rate revisions, New Media advertising policy, and guidelines for release of government advertisements
authorities.binds_whom: Newspapers/periodicals, TV & radio channels, and digital/web media (and their agencies) that want to carry government advertising
authorities.notes: Procurement-side, not conduct regulation — but it does change client obligations: empanelment criteria and rate/circulation-verification rules bind any media outlet seeking govt ad revenue, and the partner's slice explicitly names it. gov.in, static; robots blocks only /cbc/public/uploads/mandate/. Lower priority than the SRBs/CCPA because it binds a narrower set and only when a client opts into govt advertising.

authorities.authority: GAC — Grievance Appellate Committee(s) (MeitY)
authorities.instrument_types: Appellate orders reviewing intermediary grievance-officer decisions under IT Rules 2021, Rule 3A
authorities.binds_whom: Social-media and other intermediaries — cross-slice, but its content-restoration/removal orders can reach digital publishers and OTT
authorities.notes: Sits more in the intermediary/social-media slice than broadcast, but flagged for completeness because GAC orders can force content restoration or takedown that a media/OTT client cares about. Constituted 2022-23; orders exposed via the gac.gov.in portal (JS front-end — verify extraction path). Recommend it be owned by the social-media/intermediary slice rather than this one, but it should not fall through the cracks.

authorities.authority: MIB — Broadcasting/Cable/Uplinking-Downlinking + Broadcasting Bill
authorities.instrument_types: Acts/policies/guidelines (Uplinking & Downlinking Guidelines 2022, Cable TV Networks Rules incl. Advertising & Programme Codes), orders, advisories, and any Broadcasting Services (Regulation) Bill drafts
authorities.binds_whom: TV broadcasters, teleports/uplinking licensees, MSOs/LCOs/DTH, and (via draft Bill) potentially OTT/digital news
authorities.notes: Already covered via mib_acts_policy, mib_broadcasting, mib_orders_notices, mib_advisories and gazette_mib. No new source needed — but confirm the broadcasting-wing scrape actually lands the Uplinking/Downlinking guideline PDFs and any re-tabled Broadcasting Bill, since those are the highest-value MIB instruments for this slice.

authorities.authority: CBFC — Central Board of Film Certification
authorities.instrument_types: Certification orders, circulars, and certification guidelines
authorities.binds_whom: Film producers/distributors and theatrical/streaming release of certified films
authorities.notes: Covered. No gap. Post-Cinematograph (Amendment) Act 2023 the age-based categories (UA 7+/13+/16+) circulars flow through here — confirm the circulars lane catches them.

authorities.authority: PRGI — Press Registrar General of India (formerly RNI)
authorities.instrument_types: Advisories, public notices, registration rules under the Press and Registration of Periodicals Act 2023
authorities.binds_whom: Newspaper/periodical publishers
authorities.notes: Covered as PRGI. No gap — confirm coverage reflects the PRP Act 2023 regime (RNI superseded), which changed registration obligations for print clients.

authorities.authority: ASCI — Advertising Standards Council of India
authorities.instrument_types: Code, guidelines (influencer/'Guidelines for Influencer Advertising in Digital Media', greenwashing, etc.) and complaint outcomes/advisories
authorities.binds_whom: Advertisers, agencies, endorsers/influencers, and media carrying ads (self-reg, but referenced by CCPA/sector regulators)
authorities.notes: Covered. Note it is the self-reg twin of CCPA — keeping ASCI without CCPA is exactly the asymmetry to fix, since CCPA carries the statutory penalty power ASCI lacks.

authorities.authority: Online Gaming Authority of India (OGAI)
authorities.instrument_types: The published list/blacklist of 'online money games'; codes of practice; directions and orders (s.9); registration decisions for e-sports and online social games; grievance-appeal decisions; enforcement/coordination directions to financial institutions and law enforcement
authorities.binds_whom: Every online gaming platform, e-sports operator and online social-game operator offering to Indian users; indirectly the payment intermediaries and hosting/app-store intermediaries that carry them
authorities.notes: THE new central regulator for this whole slice, constituted under s.8 of PROGA 2025 as a digital-first attached office of MeitY (chaired by Addl. Secy MeitY, with JS-level members from MHA, DFS, MIB, MYAS, Legal Affairs). Act + Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026 notified 22 Apr 2026, in force 1 May 2026. gazette_meity catches the foundational notifications (the Act, the Rules, the s.8 constitution and s.15 investigation-officer notifications all hit the Gazette), which is why this is 'partial' not 'gap' — but OGAI's live operational stream (the codes of practice, the running list of banned money games, s.9 directions, registration grants/refusals, appeal outcomes) is digital-first on the MeitY/OGAI pages and is NOT reliably gazetted. That stream is the gap. Page confirmed HTTP 200, static template (~3KB), robots Allow:/. Note also: takedown of banned money-game apps runs through confidential MeitY s.69A blocking orders (Rule 16 IT Blocking Rules 2009) which are genuinely unpublished — a partner learns of those via client takedown/app-store delisting notices, press and IFF's blocking tracker, not from any portal.

authorities.authority: MeitY (nodal ministry — direct site, meity.gov.in)
authorities.instrument_types: Online Gaming Rules 2026 and amendments; commencement/enforcement notifications; draft rules for consultation; office memoranda, clarifications, press notes and 'what's new'; the earlier (now overtaken) 2023 IT Rules online-gaming amendment
authorities.binds_whom: All online gaming, platform and intermediary clients; the ministry that both writes the rules and hosts OGAI
authorities.notes: We hold gazette_meity, so gazette-notified rules are caught — but MeitY's own site is where the draft Rules 2025 (public-feedback version), OMs, clarifications and press notes land first, and sometimes only. A broad TMT partner cannot run gaming advice off the Gazette alone during a live rule-rollout. Concrete proof it matters: the draft Rules went up for consultation on meity.gov.in before the 22 Apr 2026 final; MeitY's 'banks as frontline gatekeepers' framing (Aug 2026) and the single-stage e-sports determination change surfaced via ministry communications, not the Gazette. Site HTTP 200, robots Allow:/. Recommend monitoring meity.gov.in notifications/whats-new as a distinct source, same way we treat other regulators directly rather than only via Gazette.

authorities.authority: State online gaming authorities — Tamil Nadu Online Gaming Authority (TNOGA) and peer state regimes (Karnataka, Telangana, AP; legacy skill-licence states Nagaland/Sikkim/Meghalaya)
authorities.instrument_types: State RMG regulations (TNOGA: blackout/'blank' hours, Aadhaar-OTP KYC, deposit/time limits, addiction warnings); state gaming/gambling prohibition Acts and ordinances; historical skill-game licences
authorities.binds_whom: Gaming operators serving residents of the relevant state
authorities.notes: Recent concrete instrument: TNOGA (Real Money Games) Regulations, 2025 notified 12 Feb 2025 (midnight-5AM curfew, mandatory Aadhaar KYC, spend limits), upheld by the Madras HC. Practitioner caveat that drives the ranking: PROGA s.18 gives the central Act overriding effect and s.5 bans ALL online money games regardless of skill/chance, so the state RMG layer is now largely superseded for live business — Karnataka is preparing an SC challenge alleging federal overreach, and the Act itself is under challenge in the Supreme Court. So track this layer for the federalism litigation, transition/legacy exposure, and residual/offline gambling powers (e.g. the Bihar Gambling Act vs PROGA conflict flagged Aug 2026), not because states still license RMG. Authoritative text sits in each State Gazette; state portals (tn.gov.in HTTP 200) carry republications.

authorities.authority: RBI / NPCI (payment-rail gatekeeping for gaming)
authorities.instrument_types: RBI circulars/directions to banks, PA-PGs and PSPs; NPCI/UPI operational circulars blocking or restricting money-game merchant categories; KYC and merchant-onboarding directions
authorities.binds_whom: Payment-intermediary clients directly; gaming/platform clients indirectly through their payment rails
authorities.notes: PROGA s.5 plus the 2026 Rules make banks and payment intermediaries 'frontline gatekeepers' — they must verify a game's legal classification before processing user funds (MeitY, Aug 2026). This is the actual enforcement chokepoint for the money-game ban, so it binds our gaming clients' cashflows even though RBI/NPCI are strictly the fintech desk's regulators. Flagging as a cross-slice touchpoint: if a fintech colleague already monitors RBI/NPCI, coordinate rather than duplicate; if not, the gaming-payment circulars are a genuine gap. rbi.org.in reachable; check robots for the notifications directory before crawling.

authorities.authority: FIU-IND / Enforcement Directorate (PMLA + offshore/crypto overlap)
authorities.instrument_types: PMLA directions and advisories to reporting entities; reporting-entity registration obligations; ED/FIU enforcement and show-cause actions against offshore money-gaming operators and VDA (crypto) exchanges
authorities.binds_whom: Gaming platforms and PA-CBs as PMLA reporting entities; crypto exchanges (VDA reporting entities); offshore operators targeting Indian users
authorities.notes: This is the fintech-crypto touchpoint the brief flags: PA-CBs must register with FIU-IND as a reporting entity before RBI authorisation, and the offshore-gaming/crypto nexus is live (ED/CBI/Interpol PIL alleging >Rs 2 lakh crore evasion via offshore operators; VDA reporting-entity regime since Mar 2023). Relevant to gaming clients running real-money or crypto-settled products and to any platform with an offshore arm. Caveat: many FIU directions to individual reporting entities are not publicly posted (effectively unpublished) — a partner learns of them via the client's own compliance notices, ED press releases and litigation, so treat the public site as partial signal only.

authorities.authority: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports / Department of Sports (e-sports nodal ministry)
authorities.instrument_types: E-sports recognition and promotion notifications; the multi-sport-event recognition; e-sports eligibility/registration framework operated jointly with OGAI
authorities.binds_whom: E-sports operators, organisers and leagues — the promoted/permitted category left standing after the money-game ban
authorities.notes: The Act splits administration: MeitY/OGAI for gaming generally, MIB for online social games, and MYAS/Department of Sports as the e-sports nodal ministry (building on the Dec 2022 President's amendment recognising e-sports as a multi-sport event). E-sports registration itself now runs under OGAI per the 2026 Rules, but eligibility and promotion flow through MYAS. Smaller client base than RMG, but e-sports is the one growth lane a gaming client can still legally pursue, so a broad TMT partner tracks it. yas.gov.in HTTP 200, static, likely clean.

authorities.authority: CBIC / GST Council (28% GST on online money gaming)
authorities.instrument_types: CBIC rate notifications and circulars; GST Council decisions on valuation of online gaming supplies
authorities.binds_whom: Online money-gaming operators (historically) and surviving permitted categories; a live retro-demand exposure for legacy operators
authorities.notes: 28% GST on full face value of bets (effective Oct 2023) was the sector's existential tax issue and the retrospective show-cause demands are still in Supreme Court litigation. Squarely the tax team's source, not a TMT regulator — flag it so the gaming-practice partner knows the exposure exists and routes it, rather than owning it. Forward relevance narrows post-ban (money games gone), but legacy demands persist. cbic-gst.gov.in publishes notifications as static PDFs.

authorities.authority: Industry self-regulatory / federation bodies (AIGF, E-Gaming Federation, FIFS) and the never-notified MeitY SRB mechanism
authorities.instrument_types: Voluntary codes of ethics/conduct binding members only; the 2023 IT-Rules 'online gaming self-regulatory body' framework that was never operationalised
authorities.binds_whom: Only voluntary members; no statutory reach
authorities.notes: Included so the partner knows this is dead, not missing. MeitY's 2023 online-gaming SRB scheme never had a single SRB notified and is now overtaken by OGAI, which is a statutory regulator rather than an industry SRO. AIGF/EGF/FIFS are lobbying/standard-setting associations, not regulators — worth a light watch for industry-position signals (esp. around the SC challenge) but they issue nothing that binds a non-member client. Distinct from PRGI, which we already cover for press/media.

authorities.authority: ASCI (gaming advertising self-regulation) — already covered
authorities.instrument_types: Guidelines for advertising of online real-money gaming (mandatory disclaimers, restrictions); advisories against surrogate/illegal betting ads
authorities.binds_whom: Gaming and platform advertisers (self-regulatory, with MIB backstop)
authorities.notes: Listed for slice completeness: the gaming-advertising dimension is already caught via our ASCI source. With the money-game ban, ASCI's RMG-ad guidelines shift toward policing surrogate/offshore betting ads. The statutory ad-ban enforcement (PROGA prohibits advertising online money games) flows through OGAI/MIB, which our OGAI-gap and existing MIB coverage address — no new source needed here beyond confirming ASCI stays in scope.

authorities.authority: MIB (online social games administration + betting-ad advisories) — already covered
authorities.instrument_types: Administration of 'online social games' category under the Act; advisories to media/OTT/social platforms against betting and money-game advertising/surrogates
authorities.binds_whom: Broadcasters, OTT and social-media intermediaries carrying gaming/betting content and ads
authorities.notes: Listed for completeness: the Act names MIB as administering authority for online social games, and MIB is our existing source (mib_advisories, mib_orders_notices, mib_digital_media). Its recurring betting/surrogate-ad advisories to broadcasters and platforms are the gaming-relevant output and are already in-tracker. No gap — but worth a note that MIB's role now carries a specific gaming mandate, so the gaming partner should read MIB output through that lens.

authorities.authority: CCI — Competition Commission of India
authorities.instrument_types: Combination approval/rejection orders (s.31), abuse-of-dominance & anti-competitive-agreement orders (s.27), regulations (CCI (Combination) Regs 2024, Settlement Regs 2024, Commitment Regs 2024, Determination of Turnover/Income Regs 2024, General Regs), guidance notes, market study reports, weekly register of notified combinations
authorities.binds_whom: Every TMT client doing M&A/JV/investment needing merger clearance (telecom, OTT/platforms, media, e-commerce, gaming, device makers) and any dominant digital platform facing abuse cases
authorities.notes: The single most embarrassing gap for a deals partner. Deal Value Threshold (INR 2,000 cr + 'substantial business operations in India') live since 10 Sep 2024 under CCI (Combination) Regs 2024 — now catches sub-threshold tech/digital acquisitions that used to escape review. Proof it bites: CCI's INR 213.14 cr penalty on Meta/WhatsApp (18 Nov 2024) over the 2021 privacy-policy data-sharing, plus ongoing Google Play/Android matters. robots.txt blocks only some /images/ dirs (pre-filing consultations are confidential by design); published orders and the weekly combination register are fully open. /antitrust/orders and /combination both show live 2025-2026 orders.

authorities.authority: DPIIT — Dept for Promotion of Industry & Internal Trade (Min. of Commerce & Industry)
authorities.instrument_types: FDI Press Notes, annual Consolidated FDI Policy Circular, sectoral clarifications and Office Memoranda
authorities.binds_whom: Any TMT client taking foreign investment: telecom (100%, security-conditioned), broadcasting/DTH/cable/FM/uplink-downlink caps, digital news media (26%), e-commerce marketplace (100% with inventory barred and Press Note 2/2018 conditions), satellite/space comms
authorities.notes: robots is 'Allow: /' but the relaunched DPIIT site is an SPA shell (7KB, no press-note text in raw HTML) — the PN PDFs load via API; the same press notes are also gazette_recoverable and republished as standalone PDFs. Recent proof: Press Note 1 of 2024 liberalised space-sector FDI (satellites/launch vehicles/components) — direct to satellite-comms clients. IMPORTANT nuance for the pipeline: our existing e-Gazette lanes are ministry-scoped to Communications/MeitY/MIB and do NOT capture DPIIT (Commerce) notifications, so 'gazette is covered' does not close this gap. The enforceable cap ultimately lives in the FEMA NDI Rules (see RBI/DEA row); the press note is policy until the rule amendment lands.

authorities.authority: MCA — Ministry of Corporate Affairs
authorities.instrument_types: Notifications commencing Competition (Amendment) Act 2023 provisions, exemption notifications (de-minimis/small-target, target exemption), Competition Act rules; Companies Act notifications/rules on schemes and compliance; custodian of the draft Digital Competition Bill
authorities.binds_whom: Sets the merger-control perimeter for all TMT dealmakers (thresholds, exemptions, DVT/global-turnover commencement); Companies Act reaches every incorporated TMT client
authorities.notes: mca.gov.in returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients (bot-protected), so a scraper needs a headless browser OR should recover MCA notifications from the Gazette — but note again our Gazette lanes stop at Communications/MeitY/MIB and do not include Corporate Affairs. Concrete: the Sep 2024 MCA notification that commenced the Deal Value Threshold and the de-minimis/target exemption is what actually switched the CCI regime on. This is where the perimeter changes are notified, upstream of CCI itself.

authorities.authority: DGFT — Directorate General of Foreign Trade (Min. of Commerce & Industry)
authorities.instrument_types: Foreign Trade Policy, Notifications (import policy / HS-code restrictions), Public Notices (procedure), Trade Notices, import authorisation / import management systems
authorities.binds_whom: Device makers, telecom-gear importers, OEMs, data-centre/server importers, CCTV/IP-camera vendors
authorities.notes: The /CP portal serves full HTML notification and public-notice lists with 2025 and 2026 entries present (no robots.txt at all — public govt portal). Concrete proof: the IT-Hardware Import Management System for HSN 8471 (laptops/tablets/servers), originating in Notification 23/2023, was continued/extended into 2025 requiring import authorisation — a direct on/off switch for hardware clients' ability to import. Recurring restrictions also hit telecom/CCTV items. Like DPIIT, DGFT is Commerce-ministry and not caught by our current gazette lanes.

authorities.authority: NCLAT — National Company Law Appellate Tribunal
authorities.instrument_types: Appellate judgments and daily orders on CCI decisions (and Companies Act / IBC appeals)
authorities.binds_whom: Any TMT client appealing or affected by a CCI combination or abuse order — a CCI order is not settled law until NCLAT (then Supreme Court)
authorities.notes: Drupal site; robots is standard (only admin/user/search paths disallowed), judgment/order pages open. This is the sister of our existing TDSAT coverage: we track the telecom tribunal but not the competition appellate tier. Proof it changes the client's actual obligation: NCLAT (23 Jan 2025) stayed CCI's 5-year data-sharing ban on Meta/WhatsApp pending appeal — the operative restraint on the client moved at the appellate stage, not the CCI stage.

authorities.authority: RBI / FEMA Non-Debt Instruments Rules (rule-maker: MoF — Dept of Economic Affairs)
authorities.instrument_types: FEMA (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules amendments (DEA), RBI A.P. (DIR Series) circulars, Master Direction on Foreign Investment, FEMA notifications; FDI reporting via FIRMS/SMF
authorities.binds_whom: Every TMT client receiving FDI — the NDI Rules are where the DPIIT sector caps/conditions become enforceable law; entry route, pricing, reporting all sit here
authorities.notes: rbi.org.in ASPX notification pages return full HTML (113KB). The practitioner point: a DPIIT press note only bites once mirrored into the NDI Rules by a DEA amendment (e.g., space-sector liberalisation had to be carried into the NDI Rules). A partner tracks the rule/circular, not just the press note — so this pairs with the DPIIT row rather than duplicating it. RBI has site terms/copyright; verify before bulk fetch.

authorities.authority: BIS — Bureau of Indian Standards (Compulsory Registration Scheme)
authorities.instrument_types: CRS orders/notifications, product-inclusion notifications, Quality Control Orders bringing electronics/telecom goods under mandatory registration
authorities.binds_whom: Device makers and importers — phones, laptops, wireless gear, IoT, adapters must be BIS-registered to be sold or imported in India
authorities.notes: crsbis.in/BIS returns a 62-byte JS shell (portal is app-rendered); the CRS product list and orders are PDFs on bis.gov.in / the CRS portal. Adjacency to note: some standards flow via the MeitY gazette (partially covered), but the CRS inclusion orders themselves are BIS instruments and are a genuine gap. Matters because a hardware client's ability to import/sell turns on the current CRS product list, which keeps expanding to new electronics/telecom categories.

authorities.authority: Digital Competition Bill / Committee on Digital Competition Law (MCA)
authorities.instrument_types: Draft Digital Competition Bill, CDCL committee report, and the future ex-ante regulations that would designate Systemically Significant Digital Enterprises (SSDEs) with pre-emptive do's/don'ts
authorities.binds_whom: Large digital platforms (search, social, ad-tech, app stores, e-commerce, cloud) that would face ex-ante obligations instead of ex-post CCI cases
authorities.notes: Distinct watch-item stream (kept separate from the MCA row because it is a pipeline of consultation drafts, not yet an operative instrument). MCA released the draft Bill and CDCL report in Mar 2024; not yet enacted. A platform partner tracks its progress because it would flip platform obligations from ex-post enforcement to ex-ante compliance — importance jumps to high the moment it is notified. Until then it is a consultation/press item, not law online.

authorities.authority: NCLT — National Company Law Tribunal
authorities.instrument_types: Orders sanctioning schemes of arrangement/amalgamation (Companies Act s.230-232), oppression & mismanagement orders, cause lists
authorities.binds_whom: TMT clients executing mergers/demergers by court-approved scheme — deal structure and timing, separate from CCI clearance
authorities.notes: nclt.gov.in rejects plain curl (HTTP 400 — needs browser headers). Relevant to deal-execution mechanics rather than obligation-changing rule-making, so lower priority than NCLAT for this competition/FDI slice. Include only if the tracker wants deal-plumbing coverage; a broad TMT partner would rarely be embarrassed to miss a specific NCLT scheme order compared to a CCI/DPIIT change.

authorities.authority: CBIC / Customs — tariff on telecom & electronics
authorities.instrument_types: Customs tariff notifications, IGCR rules, exemptions/PMP duty changes on telecom & electronics inputs
authorities.binds_whom: Device makers and importers — affects duty/landed cost of phones, components, telecom gear
authorities.notes: Lowest priority in this slice: changes hardware economics (e.g., annual Budget duty tweaks on phone components / phased-manufacturing programme) but rarely changes a client's core legal obligation to operate. Flag as a candidate only if the practice wants cost/trade-duty signal; otherwise DGFT + BIS carry the import-side obligations that actually gate market access.

authorities.authority: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), Department of Consumer Affairs — consumer-protection wing (dark patterns, e-commerce rules, endorsement/influencer guidance, drip pricing)
authorities.instrument_types: CCPA guidelines (dark patterns, misleading-advertisement & endorsement), safety notices, penalty/discontinuation orders, self-audit advisories; DoCA rules & draft rules (Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules); PIB press releases carry most CCPA orders
authorities.binds_whom: e-commerce platforms & marketplaces, social-media & search intermediaries carrying paid promotions, D2C/online sellers, celebrity/influencer endorsers and virtual influencers, device & electronics sellers making performance claims
authorities.notes: Single biggest hole in the slice — reaches nearly every e-commerce/platform/influencer client. Concrete 2025 instrument: CCPA advisory of 5 June 2025 directing all e-commerce platforms to self-audit for dark patterns within 3 months and file self-declarations, on top of the Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 (13 specified patterns — drip pricing, basket-sneaking, false urgency, subscription traps). Endorsement 'Know-hows' (2023) + health/wellness influencer guidance also live here. OPERATIONAL WARNING: the old host consumeraffairs.nic.in now times out entirely; DoCA has migrated to doca.gov.in (TLS cert expired — fetch with -k). Content is a JS/portal shell with guidelines/orders as PDFs; many CCPA orders surface first via PIB, so pair the site with a PIB Consumer Affairs feed. ASCI (covered) is only the self-regulatory mirror of this — it is not a substitute for the statutory CCPA.

authorities.authority: Legal Metrology Division, Department of Consumer Affairs (Directorate of Legal Metrology + state controllers)
authorities.instrument_types: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules amendments, mandatory-declaration notifications, exemptions, clarificatory circulars/OMs; gazetted under Ministry of Consumer Affairs
authorities.binds_whom: e-commerce platforms & marketplaces (Rule-6 pre-purchase declarations on listings), device & electronics makers/importers (MRP, net quantity, country-of-origin, importer details), packaged-goods D2C sellers, quick-commerce
authorities.notes: Directly binds every product listing and every device box. Recent driver: Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Amendment Rules mandating unit-sale-price declarations (phased in 2024) and tightened e-commerce/quick-commerce declaration enforcement through 2025; per-unit and QR-declaration proposals still moving. Instruments gazette under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, which is NOT one of our three tracked Gazette ministries (Communications/MeitY/MIB) — so nothing in the current tracker catches these. Same doca.gov.in portal caveat (expired cert, PDF-driven).

authorities.authority: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) — Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) for electronics/IT hardware + Quality Control Orders
authorities.instrument_types: CRS registration mandates & product-category additions, Quality Control Orders (QCOs), Indian Standards, laboratory/registration circulars; the triggering 'Electronics & IT Goods (Requirement of Compulsory Registration) Order' is a MeitY gazette notification
authorities.binds_whom: device makers & importers (mobile phones, laptops/tablets, wearables, power banks, chargers, LED/IT hardware, IoT), e-commerce sellers of electronics (cannot list uncertified goods), component & accessory suppliers
authorities.notes: Critical for every hardware client. PARTIAL only by accident: the covered-goods list is set by MeitY's Compulsory Registration Order, whose amendments gazette under MeitY and would be caught by our gazette_meity lane — but BIS's own CRS product additions, QCO timelines, extension OMs and the registered-products database are administrative and untracked. 2025 momentum: continued CRS category expansion (new IoT/wearable and power-bank/charger lines), USB-C common-charger standardisation, smart-meter QCOs. bis.gov.in is clean WordPress (robots blocks only /wp-admin/) = easy scrape; the live registration list sits on the separate CRS portal crsbis.in (JSP, no robots.txt, session-driven).

authorities.authority: Wireless Planning & Coordination Wing (WPC), Department of Telecommunications — Equipment Type Approval (ETA) & frequency de-licensing
authorities.instrument_types: ETA (self-declaration) mandate & exemption notices, de-licensing/low-power-equipment notifications, spectrum/import-clearance circulars; radio-equipment notifications gazette under Ministry of Communications
authorities.binds_whom: makers & importers of any radio-frequency device (Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/NFC/UWB gear, phones, routers, wearables, IoT modules, drones), e-commerce sellers of wireless devices
authorities.notes: Distinct from TEC/MTCTE (which we cover) — TEC certifies telecom equipment, WPC approves radio devices; do not conflate them. PARTIAL: WPC de-licensing/ETA-mandate notifications gazette under Ministry of Communications, so gazette_communications may catch the formal notifications, but WPC circulars/OMs and the ETA database are untracked. 2025 driver: continued frequency de-licensing (indoor 6 GHz Wi-Fi delicensing debate; low-power/very-low-power device notifications) and mandatory ETA self-declaration for de-licensed-band devices. WPC pages sit on dot.gov.in (static, fetchable); the ETA self-declaration portal on eservices.dot.gov.in/saral-sanchar is login-gated and returns 403 on robots — treat as blocked/JS.

authorities.authority: Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) — E-Waste (Management) Rules / EPR for electronics producers
authorities.instrument_types: EPR registration mandates, EPR target/floor-price notifications, producer compliance directions and enforcement/show-cause orders; the E-Waste (Management) Rules gazette under MoEFCC
authorities.binds_whom: producers/importers/brand-owners of electronics & IT hardware (EEE), device makers, and increasingly online sellers of electronics with EPR obligations
authorities.notes: Every electronics/device 'producer' carries EPR registration + annual targets — a live compliance and litigation front. Concrete recent instrument: CPCB EPR floor-price notification under the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, challenged by producers in the Delhi High Court through 2024-2025. Rules themselves gazette under MoEFCC (not a tracked ministry). cpcb.gov.in robots is Disallow:/ except /web/ (so most of the main site is off-limits to a compliant crawler); the operative EPR registration/notice portal is eprewastecpcb.in (Cloudflare, JS/portal). Best clean path is the MoEFCC Gazette for the rules + PDFs served off /web/.

authorities.authority: MeitY — as issuer of the electronics CRS Order, QCOs and consumer-/device-tech notifications (beyond the Gazette lane)
authorities.instrument_types: Compulsory Registration Orders & amendments, QCOs, IT-hardware/electronics notifications, press notes, office memoranda
authorities.binds_whom: device & electronics makers/importers (via CRS scope), IT-hardware manufacturers, semiconductor/component players
authorities.notes: We already run gazette_meity, which catches MeitY's gazetted notifications — the main CRS/QCO triggers land there. The seam is MeitY's own notifications/press-note pages (office memoranda, deadline extensions, scheme circulars) that never hit the Gazette. meity.gov.in robots is 'Allow: /' (clean) but the site is now a JS/React shell — needs a rendered/API fetch, not raw HTML. Flagged 'partial' so the CRS/QCO story isn't assumed fully covered by the gazette lane alone.

authorities.authority: India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), Digital India Corporation / MeitY
authorities.instrument_types: Scheme guidelines & amendments (Semicon India / Modified schemes, DLI, ATMP/OSAT), fiscal-support approvals, application notices — incentive/approval instruments, not obligation-imposing regulation
authorities.binds_whom: semiconductor fab/ATMP/OSAT and design (DLI) applicants and hardware clients seeking incentives; not a broad obligation source
authorities.notes: Named in the brief, but be honest about altitude: ISM is an incentive/approvals office, not a regulator that changes client obligations day-to-day. Matters to hardware clients for scheme eligibility and approvals — e.g., 2025 ISM unit approvals (HCL-Foxconn OSAT JV cleared May 2025; further units under discussion) and Modified Semicon scheme terms. ism.gov.in is static HTML with no robots.txt (permissive by default) = trivially fetchable. Rank below the true obligation sources (CCPA/BIS/Legal Metrology); track for scheme-guideline changes, not for binding directions.

authorities.authority: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), Ministry of Power — Standards & Labelling (star-rating) programme
authorities.instrument_types: Mandatory/voluntary star-labelling notifications, product-category inclusions, testing & labelling schedules
authorities.binds_whom: makers/importers of covered electronics & appliances (some IT/AV/display and consumer-electronics categories), e-commerce sellers of labelled goods
authorities.notes: Relevant to device/consumer-electronics clients as categories move from voluntary to mandatory labelling (ongoing expansion through 2025). Narrower than BIS/Legal Metrology for a pure TMT book, hence moderate. beeindia.gov.in serves large static HTML (fetchable); the S&L operational portal beestarlabel.com is ASP.NET/session-driven. Track for new mandatory-labelling notifications affecting electronics.

authorities.authority: National / State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions (NCDRC and CPA-2019 fora)
authorities.instrument_types: Adjudicatory orders/judgments (platform liability, deficiency-of-service, unfair-trade-practice) — precedent, not standing obligations
authorities.binds_whom: e-commerce marketplaces/platforms, service providers, device sellers named as opposite parties; shapes platform-liability exposure sector-wide
authorities.notes: Case-law lane rather than instrument lane — a broad TMT partner watches it for evolving platform-liability and 'intermediary vs seller' precedent under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, not for rule changes. ncdrc.nic.in is a slow NIC host (timed out on test); the current live path is the e-Jagriti portal (e-jagriti.gov.in, JS-driven). Lower priority than the obligation-issuing bodies above; include if the tracker is meant to catch precedent, otherwise defer.

authorities.authority: MeitY — Section 69A blocking orders (IT Blocking Rules 2009, Rule 16 confidentiality)
authorities.url: https://www.meity.gov.in/ (orders NOT published; confidential under Rule 16)
authorities.instrument_types: Blocking orders/directions to intermediaries and licensees; interim + final directions of the Designated Officer; emergency blocking under Rule 9
authorities.binds_whom: Social-media intermediaries, ISPs/telcos, app stores, OTT/video platforms, DNS/hosting — anyone directed to disable access to content, URLs, accounts or apps
authorities.notes: The single most embarrassing thing to miss: these change a client's obligations directly yet NEVER appear on any official venue — Rule 16 makes them confidential; no gazette, no website. 2025 proof: the reported bulk order to block ~8,000 X accounts (Feb 2025) and the running s.69A account/app blocks became public ONLY through X Corp's litigation filings and press. A partner learns of them via (a) the client's own receipt of the order, (b) litigation disclosures (Shreya Singhal, Twitter/X v. UOI record), (c) RTI, and (d) trackers — MediaNama, IFF (they RTI and litigate these), SFLC.in (maintains a blocking tracker). Practical tracker design: you cannot fetch the order; you monitor the press/IFF/SFLC layer and the court dockets where they surface. Not gazette-recoverable.

authorities.authority: MHA / I4C — Sahyog portal notices (s.79(3)(b) IT Act r/w Rule 3(1)(d) IT Rules 2021)
authorities.instrument_types: Takedown/removal notices to intermediaries channelled through a govt portal; nodal-officer notifications; s.79(3)(b) 'actual knowledge' notices
authorities.binds_whom: Every significant social-media intermediary and platform operating in India (the loss-of-safe-harbour trigger); e-commerce and UGC hosts
authorities.notes: The live 2025 obligation-changer. Launched by MHA/I4C in 2024 as the notice-routing mechanism the govt is now using in preference to s.69A. Karnataka HC in X Corp v. Union of India (WP 7405/2025, judgment 24 Sep 2025) UPHELD its validity, held s.79(3)(b) grounds a takedown power distinct from s.69A, and denied X foreign-entity Art.19 standing; X has filed a writ appeal to the Division Bench. Notices themselves are portal-internal and unpublished. A partner tracks this through: the litigation (Karnataka HC docket), IFF (published the Union's submissions), SFLC.in (judgment analysis), MediaNama, and Bar & Bench/LiveLaw order reporting. The portal login page is fetchable but content is gated — monitor the case + press layer, not the portal.

authorities.authority: Supreme Court of India — TMT judgments and pending constitutional matters
authorities.instrument_types: Judgments, interim orders, directions to the Union to frame rules, transfer/tag orders consolidating HC challenges; constitution-bench references
authorities.binds_whom: All TMT clients — sets the binding law on intermediary liability, blocking, privacy, net neutrality, free speech; directions to MeitY/MIB that become clients' future obligations
authorities.notes: TDSAT is covered but the apex court is not. Date-wise judgment lists on www.sci.gov.in render server-side (200, ~139KB, scrapeable); case-status/pending-matter lookup is form-driven. robots.txt disallows only /wp-admin/. 2025 proof: Ranveer Allahbadia v. UOI (Feb-Mar 2025) — SC granted interim protection AND directed the Centre to frame a 'limited regulatory measure' for online/social-media content (Justices Surya Kant, Kotiswar Singh); plus a stream of deepfake/obscene-content PILs the SC is fielding. These orders pre-figure the next round of MeitY rulemaking, so a broad TMT partner must catch them at source. Supplement with SCObserver for pending-matter tracking. Retrieve full text via the SCI portal or IndianKanoon.

authorities.authority: Delhi High Court — TMT judgments/orders (intermediary liability, blocking, IP-blocking, deepfakes)
authorities.instrument_types: Judgments, interim injunctions, John Doe / 'Ashok Kumar' and dynamic+ website-blocking orders, ISP/DoT/MeitY blocking directions, personality-rights injunctions
authorities.binds_whom: ISPs/telcos and DoT (blocking compliance), social-media & UGC intermediaries, OTT/streaming, AI platforms, ad-tech, e-commerce
authorities.notes: The most prolific TMT bench in India — where dynamic injunctions were born and where blocking, personality-rights and now AI-copyright law is being made. No robots.txt (404 = unrestricted); the new /web/ portal serves static daily-order and judgment index pages, but filtered case/judgment search is form+captcha. 2025 proof: ANI Media v. Wikimedia Foundation (takedown + contempt over a Wikipedia page); ANI v. OpenAI (Delhi HC jurisdiction/training-data suit, 2024-25); continuing dynamic+ rogue-site blocking orders for live-sports/OTT piracy that bind every ISP; and the Chaitanya Rohilla deepfake PIL pushing MeitY toward a deepfake framework. Fastest catch is LiveLaw/Bar & Bench (they publish the order copies same day) cross-checked against the HC portal / IndianKanoon.

authorities.authority: Karnataka High Court — TMT judgments (blocking transparency, Sahyog, s.69A/s.79)
authorities.instrument_types: Judgments and interim orders on platform takedowns, blocking-order transparency, safe-harbour scope
authorities.binds_whom: Social-media intermediaries and platforms; DoT/ISPs on blocking compliance; sets precedent on the s.69A-vs-s.79(3)(b) blocking architecture
authorities.notes: The court that owns the blocking-law line: Twitter v. UOI (2023, dismissed with Rs.50L costs — the seminal s.69A blocking-transparency loss) and now X Corp v. UOI (WP 7405/2025, 24 Sep 2025) upholding the Sahyog portal — the single most important intermediary judgment of 2025, now under writ appeal. Direct site was unreachable from here (SSL/anti-bot, returned 000), so this court is best pulled via the eCourts judgment portal and IndianKanoon rather than the HC site itself; order copies land first on LiveLaw/Bar & Bench and analysis on SFLC.in/IFF.

authorities.authority: Bombay High Court — TMT judgments (IT Rules challenges, OTT, Fact Check Unit)
authorities.instrument_types: Judgments, interim orders, constitutional rulings striking/upholding IT Rules provisions
authorities.binds_whom: Social-media intermediaries, digital news publishers, OTT/streaming; shapes IT Rules 2021/2023 obligations nationally
authorities.notes: Where the IT Rules get constitutionally tested. Kunal Kamra v. UOI: Bombay HC struck down the Fact Check Unit amendment (Rule 3(1)(b)(v), IT Amendment Rules 2023) as unconstitutional via the Sept 2024 tie-breaker judgment (J. Chandurkar) — directly removed a compliance obligation from every intermediary, with 2025 follow-on. Also active on OTT/obscenity and digital-news matters. Direct HC site failed to connect from here (SSL/000); retrieve via eCourts + IndianKanoon, with same-day order copies from LiveLaw/Bar & Bench.

authorities.authority: Madras High Court — TMT judgments (online gaming, blocking, VPN)
authorities.instrument_types: Judgments and interim orders on real-money-gaming regulation, website/app blocking, platform compliance
authorities.binds_whom: Real-money/online-gaming operators, payment and platform intermediaries, ISPs; increasingly OTT and app stores
authorities.notes: The gaming-regulation battleground. 2025 proof: challenges by Head Digital Works (A23), Junglee Games and others to the Tamil Nadu Online Gaming Authority regulations (Oct 2024) — 'blank hours' (12am-5am) and Aadhaar/KYC mandates — heard through 2025; these directly set operating obligations for every RMG client and feed into the national online-gaming debate. The /judis/ portal serves static judgment pages (200) and has no restrictive robots; cross-check eCourts/IndianKanoon. Relevant given the practice's gaming exposure.

authorities.authority: DoT / MeitY / MHA — letter-form and executive directions (unpublished)
authorities.url: not published centrally (licence-condition letters, ministry advisories/letters)
authorities.instrument_types: Licence-amendment letters, DoT directions to TSPs, MeitY advisories/letters to intermediaries, state/MHA blocking or lawful-intercept letters
authorities.binds_whom: Telcos/ISPs (licence conditions), social-media & AI intermediaries (advisory-driven obligations e.g. deepfake labelling), device makers
authorities.notes: The 'letter layer' that changes obligations without a gazette: DoT amends licence terms and issues directions by letter to operators; MeitY issues advisories/letters to intermediaries (e.g. the 2024-25 deepfake/synthetic-media labelling advisories that pushed platforms to act ahead of any rule). Some MeitY advisories surface on meity.gov.in, but most letters reach the public only when a recipient or a reporter publishes them. A partner catches these via the client, MediaNama and ET Telecom (which routinely obtain and publish DoT/MeitY letters), and IFF. Treat as a press-monitored signal, not a fetchable official source.

authorities.authority: LiveLaw — litigation reporting (SC + HC order/judgment copies)
authorities.instrument_types: Same-day reporting of court orders and judgments, with linked PDF copies; case-filing and hearing updates
authorities.binds_whom: Indirect — the acquisition channel through which TMT clients' court-driven obligations first become knowable
authorities.notes: The fastest reliable feed for court output across SC and all four HCs — usually publishes the order copy the same day, ahead of the court portals. robots.txt is Allow: / (blocks only search/preview/admin paths). This is the realistic primary sensor for the judicial layer: filter its tech/media beat for X Corp, Sahyog, blocking, IT Rules, deepfake, gaming and net-neutrality tags, then pull the underlying order. Pair with Bar & Bench for redundancy.

authorities.authority: Bar & Bench — litigation reporting (SC + HC)
authorities.instrument_types: Court-order and judgment reporting with PDF copies; hearing/filing updates; interviews signalling pending matters
authorities.binds_whom: Indirect — court-driven obligation channel for all TMT clients
authorities.notes: Co-equal to LiveLaw as a litigation tracker; frequently first on interim orders. It carried the Karnataka HC 'X Corp denied interim relief / Sahyog' reporting and the subsequent appeal. robots.txt is Allow: / with sitemaps exposed — clean to monitor. Running both LiveLaw and Bar & Bench de-risks single-source lag on the fast-moving judicial layer.

authorities.authority: MediaNama — tech-policy tracker (blocking, s.69A, Sahyog, IT Rules)
authorities.instrument_types: Investigative/explanatory reporting on blocking orders, takedown notices, consultations, licence and rule changes; often reproduces the underlying document
authorities.binds_whom: Indirect — the best single sensor for the unpublished executive layer that binds intermediaries, telcos and platforms
