authorities.notes: The premier India digital-policy tracker and, in practice, the earliest public signal for s.69A/Sahyog/blocking events that have no official venue. robots.txt now carries a Cloudflare Content-Signal (search=yes, ai-train=no, use=reference) — a rights reservation aimed at AI training; a monitoring tracker that stores headlines/links for reference sits in a grey zone and some depth is paywalled, so flag for a terms check before automated ingestion. Even if only headline-monitored, it is the highest-yield gap-filler for the unpublished layer.

authorities.authority: Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) — digital-rights litigation & RTI tracker
authorities.instrument_types: Litigation trackers, RTI-obtained blocking data, case documents (petitions, govt submissions), explainers
authorities.binds_whom: Indirect — surfaces the blocking/Sahyog/deepfake instruments that bind intermediaries and ISPs
authorities.notes: IFF is often a party or intervenor and publishes primary documents others don't — e.g. it posted the Union's submissions in X Corp v. UOI and maintains blocking/censorship trackers built on RTI. High practitioner value, BUT robots.txt explicitly Disallows ClaudeBot and Claude-Web (and most bots) across the whole site — automated fetching is off-limits. Treat as a manual/newsletter-monitored source, or reach the same documents through the court record and secondary coverage.

authorities.authority: eCourts — unified judgment & case-status portal (SC + High Courts)
authorities.instrument_types: Full-text judgment/order search and case-status across the SC and all HCs (Delhi/Karnataka/Bombay/Madras)
authorities.binds_whom: Indirect — the canonical retrieval backbone for the judicial layer, especially the two HCs whose own sites are hard to fetch
authorities.notes: The official free aggregator that reaches Karnataka and Bombay HC (whose direct sites failed to connect here) plus Delhi, Madras and the SC from one place. Both endpoints return 200 but search is captcha-gated and session-driven (no clean API; no meaningful robots.txt), so ingestion needs a headless/captcha path — a build cost, not a legal blocker per se, but automated access terms are unclear, hence check_robots. Best used as the authoritative back-fill once a press signal names a case.

authorities.authority: IndianKanoon — free full-text judgment search (SC + HC)
authorities.instrument_types: Indexed, searchable full text of SC and HC judgments/orders; citation graph
authorities.binds_whom: Indirect — the practitioner-default retrieval layer for judgments across all four HCs and the SC
authorities.notes: The fastest way to pull and keyword-monitor TMT judgments — plain static HTML doc pages (200), full-text search, better indexed than the court portals for tags like 'Section 69A', 'intermediary', 'Section 79'. Third-party (not official), and robots.txt disallows /cached/ and a list of specific doc IDs while allowing general crawl — so respect those and rate-limit. Ideal companion to eCourts: search here, cite the official copy.

authorities.authority: SFLC.in (Software Freedom Law Centre) — blocking/legal-analysis tracker
authorities.instrument_types: Blocking-order and internet-shutdown trackers, RTI data, judgment analyses, legal explainers
authorities.binds_whom: Indirect — documents the s.69A/blocking and platform-liability instruments that bind intermediaries and ISPs
authorities.notes: Maintains long-running blocking/shutdown trackers and publishes close analyses — e.g. its detailed breakdown of the X Corp v. UOI (Sahyog) judgment. robots.txt is standard-clean (only /wp-admin/ disallowed) with sitemap + RSS exposed, so it is straightforward to monitor. Overlaps with IFF but is legally fetchable where IFF is not, making it the more ingestible of the two civil-society trackers.

authorities.authority: Storyboard18 — media/broadcast/advertising & OTT policy tracker
authorities.instrument_types: Reporting on MIB/broadcast orders, ASCI actions, OTT and advertising regulation, gaming-ad rules, TMT litigation
authorities.binds_whom: Indirect — surfaces broadcaster, OTT, advertiser and gaming obligations from the MIB/ASCI/court side
authorities.notes: Strong on the media/advertising/broadcast slice a broad TMT partner also carries — MIB advisories, self-regulation, surrogate/real-money-gaming ad crackdowns, OTT content disputes. robots.txt Allows general crawling but blocks named AI bots (GPTBot/CCBot etc.) and has news sitemaps; a general monitor is fine but flag the AI-bot carve-outs before ingestion. Complements the litigation trackers on the content/broadcast axis rather than the blocking axis.

authorities.authority: ET Telecom (ETTelecom) — telecom/DoT policy news
authorities.instrument_types: Reporting on DoT directions, licence changes, TRAI actions, spectrum/telecom-policy letters, often reproducing letters
authorities.binds_whom: Indirect — earliest public signal for DoT/telecom licence-letter obligations binding telcos and ISPs
authorities.notes: The go-to feed for the telecom-executive layer — DoT licence-amendment letters and directions frequently break here before (or instead of) any official posting, filling the 'letter directions' gap on the telco side. robots.txt is Allow: / with several disallowed paths, but some content sits behind the ETPrime paywall and Times-group ToS apply, so check terms before automated ingestion. Headline-monitor for DoT/MeitY letter events, then chase the primary document.

authorities.authority: TDSAT — Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal
authorities.instrument_types: Judgments and daily orders; notices/circulars
authorities.binds_whom: Telcos/ISPs, broadcasters/DTH, and appeals from TRAI — binding on the telecom & broadcasting client base
authorities.notes: Already in the tracker (tdsat_orders = judgments/daily orders; tdsat_notices = notices/circulars) — logged here only to close the ledger for the judicial slice. No action needed; it is the one covered node in this slice, and the four HCs + SC + the unpublished executive layer are the real gaps around it.

plan.verdict: Yes — and the gaps are serious for a broad practice. The 43 live sources plus the three-ministry Gazette are a strong spine for TRAI/TEC/CERT-In/MIB and for GAZETTED media-telecom law, but they systematically miss the two layers where TMT obligations actually move first: (a) the non-gazetted 'own-website' output of the biggest regulators (MeitY advisories/AI guidelines/draft rules/OMs; DoT licence amendments/OMs/spectrum NIAs; CCPA dark-pattern orders; OGAI's operational stream), and (b) the entire competition/FDI and judicial layer (CCI, DPIIT, the Supreme Court and the four most active High Courts) — of which only TDSAT is covered. Four of these are the classic 'embarrassing to learn from the client' regulators. The single highest-leverage fact: the registry already holds five discovered-but-parked endpoints at status needs_decision — meity_gazettes, meity_acts_policies, meity_orders_notices, meity_guidelines and pib_moc — so the top MeitY gap can be closed by a promote decision, not a build. A distinct blind spot (s.69A blocking, Sahyog notices, GAC orders, licence letters) cannot be fixed by adding sources at all and must be handled honestly as a client-intake/litigation-watch limit.

must_add.authority: MeitY — own website (meity.gov.in) non-gazetted layer + PIB (MeitY/MHA) RSS signal lane
must_add.why: The #1 and most embarrassing gap. gazette_meity (live) catches the FINAL notified rule (DPDP Rules 14 Nov 2025; IT synthetic-content/SGI-labelling amendment Feb 2026) but misses everything that hits clients first and never gazettes: the India AI Governance Guidelines (5 Nov 2025), the 2023-24 deepfake/GenAI due-diligence advisories, consultation drafts (Oct 2025 SGI/AI-deepfake draft), s.79 letters and GAC/blocking administrative notices. Binds every intermediary, SSMI, OTT, gaming and AI/GenAI deployer and — via DPDP — every data fiduciary. CRITICAL EFFICIENCY POINT: the 4 meity_* endpoints AND pib_moc are already discovered in registry_v2.json but parked at status needs_decision — promoting them (PIB is the fastest public trace of s.69A/app-ban actions and draft press notes) is a decision, not a build, and closes most of the non-gazetted-advisory gap in this whole slice.
must_add.reachable: js_or_api — Next.js SPA with __NEXT_DATA__/WP-JSON returning clean JSON; instrument PDFs served static at /static/uploads/; PIB is a clean RSS feed already in the robots snapshot
must_add.legal: likely_clean — robots 'Allow: /' for both meity.gov.in and pib.gov.in; endpoints already scoped in-registry

must_add.authority: DoT — own website (dot.gov.in): licensing/circulars/OMs stream + /spectrum auction NIAs
must_add.why: The single biggest telecom hole. We catch DoT ONLY via ministry-wise Gazette (Communications); a large share of obligation-changing output is never gazetted or lands days/weeks earlier on-site: Unified Licence / UL-VNO / ISP / ILD licence-condition amendments, OMs, clarifications, LoIs, M&A/transfer approvals, procedural circulars, RoW clarificatory circulars, and spectrum-auction NIAs + corrigenda + pre-bid clarifications (e.g. the 8 Mar 2024 NIA, ~Rs 96,317 cr reserve — terms clients bid on). Binds the core telco/ISP/VNO/ILDO/infra base; a telecom partner would be embarrassed to learn of a UL amendment or NIA corrigendum from the client. Not in the registry at all (only dot_eservices_import is scaffolded/planned).
must_add.reachable: js_or_api — SPA listing needs a headless render / backend-API discovery, but the actual instrument PDFs are static and directly fetchable (verified 200) at /static/uploads/ and /sites/default/files/

must_add.authority: CCPA — Central Consumer Protection Authority (Dept of Consumer Affairs, doca.gov.in)
must_add.why: The biggest advertising/consumer gap and the statutory teeth that ASCI (which we cover) lacks — keeping ASCI without CCPA is exactly the asymmetry to fix. Reaches nearly every advertiser, e-commerce/marketplace, influencer/endorser, D2C seller and any broadcaster/OTT carrying ads. Very live: Dark Patterns Guidelines 2023 (13 specified patterns); 5 Jun 2025 self-audit advisory in force to 31 Dec 2026; ~9 platforms penalised 2025-26 (Zepto, BookMyShow, IndiGo, PhysicsWallah, FirstCry, SpiceJet). Sits under DoCA — NOT one of our three tracked Gazette ministries, so genuinely invisible to the tracker today.
must_add.reachable: static_html / js-portal — orders at ccpa-orders.php and doca.gov.in/ccpa/orders-advisories.php as PDFs; many CCPA orders surface first via PIB, so pair with a PIB Consumer Affairs feed
must_add.legal: likely_clean, BUT the host migrated from consumeraffairs.nic.in to doca.gov.in and the TLS cert is expired — fetch with -k

must_add.why: The most embarrassing gap for a deals partner. The Deal Value Threshold (Rs 2,000 cr + 'substantial business operations in India') live since 10 Sep 2024 now catches sub-threshold tech/digital acquisitions that used to escape review — it bites every TMT M&A/JV/investment. Enforcement is real: Rs 213.14 cr Meta/WhatsApp penalty (18 Nov 2024); ongoing Google Play/Android matters. Published combination and abuse orders plus the weekly combination register are fully open. Not in the registry.
must_add.reachable: static_html — /combination and /antitrust/orders show live 2025-26 orders and the weekly register
must_add.legal: likely_clean — robots blocks only some /images/ dirs; pre-filing consultations are confidential by design, published orders are open

must_add.authority: Judicial layer — Supreme Court + Delhi / Karnataka / Bombay / Madras High Courts (via SCI & Delhi portals + eCourts/IndianKanoon, fastest via LiveLaw + Bar & Bench)
must_add.why: TDSAT is the ONLY covered judicial node; the apex court and the four most active TMT benches make the binding law on intermediary liability, blocking, privacy, gaming and IP/AI-copyright, and issue directions to MeitY/MIB that become clients' next obligations. 2025 proof: SC Ranveer Allahbadia (directed the Centre to frame content regulation); Karnataka HC X Corp v UOI upholding Sahyog (24 Sep 2025, under writ appeal); Bombay HC striking the Fact Check Unit (Kunal Kamra, Sep 2024); Delhi HC dynamic+ blocking, ANI v OpenAI and ANI v Wikimedia; Madras HC TNOGA gaming challenges. A broad TMT partner must catch these at source.
must_add.reachable: static_html for SCI judgment-date lists and the Delhi HC /web/ index; Karnataka/Bombay HC direct sites are anti-bot (HTTP 000) so pull via eCourts + IndianKanoon; same-day order copies via LiveLaw/Bar & Bench
must_add.legal: likely_clean for SCI/Delhi/IndianKanoon plain fetch (respect IndianKanoon /cached/ disallows); eCourts is captcha-gated — a build cost, not a legal blocker

must_add.authority: OGAI — Online Gaming Authority of India, operational instrument stream (MeitY/OGAI pages)
must_add.why: THE new central regulator for the entire gaming slice, constituted under PROGA 2025 (Rules notified 22 Apr 2026, in force 1 May 2026). gazette_meity catches the foundational notifications (Act, Rules, s.8 constitution) — hence 'partial' — but OGAI's live stream (codes of practice, the running list of banned 'online money games', s.9 directions, registration grants/refusals, appeal outcomes) is digital-first and NOT reliably gazetted. A partner cannot run gaming advice off the Gazette alone during the live rollout.

plan.unpublished_layer: A real slice of what binds TMT clients never appears on any official venue, and no crawler can fix that — it must be stated as a limit, not hidden as coverage. The confidential-by-design instruments: s.69A blocking orders (MeitY Designated Officer / IT Blocking Rules 2009, Rule 16 confidentiality — never gazetted or posted; the ~8,000-account X order of Feb 2025 surfaced only via litigation); Sahyog s.79(3)(b) takedown notices (MHA/I4C — portal-internal, visible only to the served intermediary; sahyog.mha.gov.in returns HTTP 000 to non-onboarded); GAC appellate orders under Rule 3A (60,147 appeals received / 11,197 disposed as of 27 Aug 2026, but NO public orders repository — each order behind OTP+captcha, which must not be bypassed; only the aggregate counters and the constitution/reconstitution notifications are public); the DoT/MeitY/MHA 'letter layer' (licence-amendment letters, ministry advisories/letters to intermediaries, lawful-intercept/blocking letters); the Trusted-Telecom no-procurement designation lists; FIU-IND directions to individual reporting entities; and TERM-cell EMF/enforcement actions. The ONLY nets: (1) client intake — the served client tells you, which is why an intake trigger is the real primary sensor; (2) litigation watch — court dockets and filings (X Corp v UOI Karnataka HC; Shreya Singhal; Kunal Kamra) pulled same-day from LiveLaw and Bar & Bench and back-filled via eCourts/IndianKanoon; (3) specialist press and civil-society trackers — MediaNama and ET Telecom (which routinely obtain and publish DoT/MeitY letters), SFLC.in (legally fetchable, maintains blocking trackers), platform transparency reports, and IFF (high value but robots explicitly disallows ClaudeBot/Claude-Web — manual/newsletter only, or reach the same documents via the court record); and (4) RTI + Parliament answers + PIB aggregate figures. The enabling rule/constitution TEXT underneath each of these is gazette-recoverable even when the orders are not, so track the perimeter and treat the orders as a monitored blind spot.
out_of_scope_decisions: State-level breadth: whether — and how deep — to track state online-gaming/gambling regimes (TNOGA and peers) and state RoW nodal regimes. PROGA s.18 gives the central Act overriding effect and s.5 bans all online money games regardless of skill, so the state RMG layer is largely superseded for live business; it now matters chiefly for federalism litigation (Karnataka's mooted SC challenge), transition/legacy exposure, and residual/offline gambling powers (e.g. the Bihar Gambling Act vs PROGA conflict). Authoritative text sits in each State Gazette, which is a large breadth-vs-cost call only the partner can make.

Fintech depth and desk boundary: how far to go on RBI / NPCI / FEMA NDI Rules / FIU-IND — whether the TMT tracker OWNS the gaming payment-rail and VDA/PMLA circulars or coordinates with a fintech desk that may already monitor rbi.org.in, to avoid duplication.

Judicial breadth and depth: which High Courts beyond Delhi to ingest directly, whether to add deal-plumbing (NCLT scheme orders) and consumer precedent (NCDRC / e-Jagriti), and how much to rely on LiveLaw/Bar & Bench headline monitoring versus building captcha-gated primary-portal ingestion.

Terms/ToS risk appetite for automated ingestion: MediaNama's Cloudflare Content-Signal (ai-train=no), IFF's robots disallowing ClaudeBot, ETPrime/Times-group ToS, eCourts captcha, and the UIDAI / cybercrime.gov.in access walls — a legal call on exactly where to draw the automated-fetch line versus manual/newsletter monitoring.

Product-regulatory scope: whether device/hardware market-access sources (BIS CRS, Legal Metrology, DGFT, CPCB E-Waste, BEE star-labelling, BIS QCOs) belong in this TMT book or a separate product-regulatory desk — they gate market access but sit at the edge of a pure TMT practice.

Tax-adjacent exposure routing: CBIC 28%-GST-on-gaming and Customs tariff on electronics change client economics and carry live retro-demand litigation, but are the tax team's sources — flag-and-route, or own them?

Cross-desk ownership of shared nodes so nothing double-runs or falls through: GAC (intermediary slice), CCI/NCLAT/MCA (deals desk), CCPA/Legal Metrology (advertising/consumer desk). Decide who owns each.

Whether to track incentive/scheme bodies that do not impose day-to-day obligations — ISM (already planned as ism_notices) and DBN scheme guidelines — for eligibility/approvals signal, or exclude them as non-regulatory.
plan.summary: The tracker's 43 live sources plus the three-ministry Gazette are a solid spine for gazetted media-telecom law, but they miss the two layers where TMT obligations actually move first — the non-gazetted 'own-website' output of MeitY, DoT, CCPA and OGAI, and the whole competition/FDI and judicial layer (CCI, DPIIT, the Supreme Court and four High Courts), of which only TDSAT is covered. The cheapest high-value move is already sitting in the registry: promote the five parked needs_decision endpoints (meity_gazettes, meity_acts_policies, meity_orders_notices, meity_guidelines, pib_moc), which closes most of the top MeitY gap by decision rather than build. Beyond those, the genuine criticals are CCPA, CCI, DPIIT, WPC, the DoT licensing stream and the judicial layer; a strong second tier covers device market-access (BIS/DGFT/Legal Metrology), the broadcast SRBs (NBDSA/BCCC/DPCGC) and the competition-perimeter bodies (NCLAT/MCA/RBI-FEMA). Finally, be honest that s.69A blocking, Sahyog notices, GAC orders and the licence-letter layer are structurally unpublished and reachable only through client intake, litigation watch and specialist press — a limit to state plainly, not a coverage line to fake.
